decisions.text: Claude Code skills and workflows reach a user repo as pointers: init writes symlinks .claude/skills/<name> and .claude/workflows/<name>.js into the installed package (node_modules/cookwright), the same mechanism Codex needs (.agents/skills/ pointers). The 2026-10-15 decision 'Claude Code users receive skills through the plugin' is superseded. Precondition before bundle init: one Claude Code session in a scratch repo measures a skill pointer into node_modules listing the skill, the same pointer dangling neither listing it nor breaking the session, and one named workflow run through a .claude/workflows/<name>.js pointer into node_modules running to its return value, since the bundle runner depends on that route.
The setup skill is named setup, as E-012 names it; a user's own skill of that name shadows it with a WARN; a later rename costs one updated row per user.

scripts/ci/fixture.sh pins create-expo-app to an exact version as one constant, prints it on the script's first output line, and the version is bumped deliberately: a harness CI that goes red on an upstream scaffold release is property-3 rot.

The README's Releases section carries the exact release order and §8's developer's-hands list follows it: npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version, commit; git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'released: YYYY-MM-DD' plus note: lines; npx cookwright changelog, commit; git push --follow-tags (pre-push runs the gate and the changelog check); npm publish. The first release after this bundle is 0.1.0.

Rule 4: the host adapters and the playbook move into the package (packages/cookwright/hosts/, packages/cookwright/docs/playbook.md, packages/cookwright/skills/): logic is imported from the package and the package is the tarball. The charter's 'one monorepo, one version number' stands; AGENTS.md's Layout follows the move.
Rule 5 and rule 4: paths.playbook becomes optional; absent means the package's own copy. A stored copy of the playbook in a user repo rots; a user who writes their own keeps the key, a chosen state.

Rule 1, rule 2 and property 4: version goes to 2 because disposition 2 changes what an existing key means, and no user is ever blocked by it: the loader applies the migration chain in memory, a version-1 file loads, every check runs, and config is WARN 'migrated in memory; run npx cookwright migrate to write it' (weak, not drift). Only a newer version FAILs, naming the package update.

Rule 1: init never refuses on the package's absence (Level 0, property 1); a pointer written before npm install is a correct link that resolves later. Only the bundle commands that build prompt pointers (status, args) refuse, with one line naming the config root, when the playbook they would point at is missing (rule 7, rule 3: a path outside the repo would be scrubbed and the prompt would point at nothing).

Rule 4, rule 1 and rule 2: a pointer's link text is compared first; ours and resolving PASS, ours and not resolving WARN 'not installed where it points (npm install)', never FAIL; missing FAIL 'run init'; other text resolving nowhere is an earlier pointer (init updated; doctor FAIL run init); a link of theirs that resolves, or a real directory, is a chosen state (skipped; WARN naming it). 'Installed' means the target resolves, never bin/cookwright.mjs alone.

Rule 3 and rule 2: the pointer target is the installed package where it is: <config root>/node_modules/cookwright, else <top>/node_modules/cookwright when hoisted; both texts are ours. The hook commands of both hosts carry the config root when it is below the top, closing the hook half of B-002 for nested roots; B-002 narrows to a linked worktree without node_modules and a package installed elsewhere.

Rule 6: the Codex adapter is built (the charter names Codex at launch; E-007's decision names its pointers) as its own session so it can be cut. Its host.hook claims only what it reads: the file carries the doctor line; trust is not measured and the line says so (rule 3).

Rule 3: the CI workflow cannot run in this bundle (no git remote, measured), and ci.workflow set now would make bundle check FAIL here (gh run list fails without a remote, check.mjs:116-124), so ci.workflow is the developer's, set with the first push. The fixture is a script measured locally; the closeout says the GitHub run is unverified.

Rule 3 and rule 2: no Windows CI job in this stage; a permanently red job is rot (property 3) and continue-on-error is a PASS with a footnote. The job lands green with the bundle that fixes B-008/B-009; backlogged there.
Rule 2: one doctor check, host.pointers, covers skills and workflows per host, required at Level 0 (setup is Level 0; a host without workflows has fewer pointers, not a FAIL). Seventeen checks.

Charter ('Levels 1 and 2 installable, flagged experimental'): every host gets the pointers its capabilities allow (bundle and the workflows need a host with workflows, so Codex gets setup only), and each SKILL.md's first line names its level and flag (bundle: Level 2, experimental).
Rule 6: Codex's 32 KiB rules cap is not added to rules.size; backlogged with the figure. No /docs-audit skill (E-003 stays open); the workflow moves and gets its pointer.

decisions.source: kickoff 2026-10-16, the Decision 1 precondition, measured in a scratch repo with one-shot Claude Code 2.1.301 sessions
decisions.text: Measured before bundle init: (1) a .claude/skills/zzz-probe symlink into node_modules/fakepkg/skills/zzz-probe was listed and invoked, the session replying the skill's own text PROBE-OK; (2) a .claude/workflows/zzz-flow.js symlink into node_modules/fakepkg/workflows/zzz-flow.js ran as the named workflow zzz-flow and returned {"probe":"FLOW-OK"}; (3) in a second scratch repo with the same two links and no node_modules, the session answered NO to the skill and NONE to any warning or error. The pointer route stands; the plugin fallback is not needed.

Rule 1 and rule 3: s1's move commit drops paths.playbook from this repo's cookwright.json, since the key is optional from s1 on and absent means the installed copy through the workspace link, so every later session's bundle args launches; §7.1 expects only the version bump and the relaid note. A plain version-1 file stays the migration's test case. The recorded s1 split text ('the three in-repo links') is corrected by plan §4.1 and §10: the links are written in their final node_modules form.

Rule 2: ownership of a pointer link is decided by its text, the way hookCommandsPast decides a hook's: ours is the shape (../)*[<rel>/]node_modules/cookwright/(skills|hosts/<host>/workflows)/<name> plus a POINTER_TEXTS_PAST list, empty in this stage; every other link is the user's, dangling or not, skipped by init and WARN in doctor, never replaced. s1 writes this repo's three links straight in the node_modules form, which resolves through the workspace link (measured), so s6 reads kept for them and wrote for setup only.

Rule 1: a path interpolated into a hook command is quoted as a shell word (shellWord in shims.mjs) with tests for spaces, quotes, $(), backticks and semicolons. Moot in this stage since disposition 16 withdraws the change; recorded for the bundle that makes it.

Rule 3: the claim that the hook commands close B-002's hook half is withdrawn. Where each host loads its settings file for a session started at the top versus in a nested config root is unmeasured, the shims look under the config root only, and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR may already be the config root. The hook commands and the shims stay as stage 2 left them; B-002 stays open, its text noting that the pointers handle a package hoisted to the top while the hooks and shims do not; the fix is backlogged with the settings-file placement to measure first.

Rule 3: every path the bundle commands print or hash is relative to the config root, as today; a package hoisted to the top yields ../../node_modules/cookwright/... paths inside the work tree, hashed from the config root; an end-to-end test covers a nested config root with the package hoisted (bundle args and status).

Rule 1 and rule 2: /setup is a loop (doctor, one remedy, doctor again, until complete or a chosen state the recipe says to explain and stop at), its recipe exhaustive by check, status and host (the Codex AGENTS.override.md case is a chosen state, not the Claude import remedy), and the QA leg invokes it on the initial readout and lets it drive migrate and init.

Rule 3 and rule 2: the ignored note says only 'ignored by git'; doctor reads an ignored, untracked pointer as WARN naming git add -f <path>; any symlinked component on a pointer's parent path makes its row skipped, refuseLinks exempting the final pointer only; a symlinkSync failure is reported after the rows and init goes on; the support claim is narrowed: only Windows is backlogged, a non-Windows filesystem refusing links is not supported in this stage and doctor reports the missing pointer as FAIL there.

Rule 2 and the charter's levels: at Level 0 only the Level 0 pointers (setup) count as drift; a missing pointer of a Level 2 piece (bundle, the workflows) is WARN 'not required at level 0', since Level 2 is installable, not required. SKILLS in hosts.mjs carries each skill's level. An opt-out lever for a Level 2 pointer a user does not want is backlogged (rule 6, wanted once).

Rule 3: a Codex hook's identity is its command and its matcher (a wrong matcher is WARN in doctor, updated by init); the Codex rules check walks from the invocation directory up through the root for AGENTS.override.md, as shadowingFiles does for Claude, reporting root-relative names.

Rule 3 and rule 6: s7 is mandatory (the state carries its phase; a scope cut is a formal plan revision, never silence); E-007, E-012 and E-013 close; E-014 stays open, narrowed to the first green GitHub run and ci.workflow set, closed by the developer after the first push; --base on an existing config is refused in s4 with a test beside --hosts, no conditional backlog line; the create-expo-app version is measured by s7 from the registry (the kickoff reading of the npx cache was not reproducible: 5.0.0 there, not 5.0.1) and nothing is claimed in the plan.

Rule 3: bundle status prints the measured form, Workflow({ name: 'bundle-phase', args }), and says 'run init' when the workflow pointer is missing; every scratch-repo measurement and the QA leg install the npm pack tarball, the published shape, never npm install <directory>; s4 also measures codex exec with node_modules removed.

Rule 3: the schema's version accepts what the loader accepts (enum [1, 2], 1 migrated in memory) with a parity test (schema versions = {CONFIG_VERSION} ∪ keys(MIGRATIONS)); 'first line' means the first body line after the frontmatter, with a test that each shipped SKILL.md opens with frontmatter holding name and description; workflowScript picks the first configured host that has workflowsDir and refuses only when none has; the QA leg expects three lines; doctor/basics.mjs (checkConfig's WARN) joins s2's surface.

Rule 3: the /setup recipe table names every line doctor emits today (rules.block newer and malformed, host.rules old Claude Code, host.hook invalid JSON, git WARN, the Codex matcher WARN, the Level 2 pointer WARN), and a line the table does not name is shown and stopped at, never improvised on.

Rule 2 and the backlog discipline: a non-Windows filesystem that refuses symbolic links is a permanent FAIL the user cannot clear in this stage, a bug by rule 2; it gets a stable backlog id (plan §9 g) rather than silence.

Rule 3 and rule 6: the Codex hook enters the work tree's top before running doctor, so its session-start readout judges from the top and misses an AGENTS.override.md in a subdirectory the session started in; the limit is stated in plan §4.4 and the README's Codex paragraph, and doctor --from <dir> is backlogged (plan §9 h), wanted once.

Rule 3: re-check 2 judged every finding resolved (30 of 30) and named two wording leftovers that reopen nothing; both are fixed in the plan after the record, without a further run: disposition 19 and §4.4 now point at §9 (g) beside the Windows item instead of 'only Windows is backlogged', and §7.5's README Codex paragraph carries the disposition-27 limit. The implement sessions read the plan at its current sha.

Rule 1 and rule 3: the codex host entry is partial until s4 (rules, an empty shadowing list, no settings or hook, no steps or checks), so a config with codex first makes doctor's host.rules and host.hook FAIL 'the check could not run' and init throw, on this branch only. Accepted until s4, which lands before anything leaves the branch and adds shadowing ['AGENTS.override.md'], the steps, the checks and rules.size's reading of the override; the whole-branch review confirms no host-first codex path remains broken.

Accepted as built: HOSTS.claude gained workflowsDir in s1 because status needs it for the pointer note, skillsDir and PACKAGE_ROOT arrive with the pointers in s3 (nothing in s1 uses them); the AGENTS.md Layout line saying .claude/ holds this repo's pointers into node_modules/cookwright stands, s6 owns the final Layout text (plan §7.5).

Rule 3: the s1 checkpoint 'bundle args stage-3 implement:s2 measured on this repo' could not be run by the implementer (the phase was not started); s1 measured implement:s1 instead (playbook node_modules/cookwright/docs/playbook.md, sha 6c4ae496f43cc3f1), and the orchestrator measures implement:s2's args when starting that phase, which is the launch itself.

Accepted as built pending the developer's strings batch: bundle status prints the missing-pointer line as a separate 'note     : …' line under 'next', a new label in the status readout; the eight s1 strings go to the developer in one batch.

Accepted as built: the single README Commands bullet for migrate landed with its commit (the doc-sync rule), and s5 reconciles it with the Updating section it writes (plan §7.5); this repo's cookwright.json stays at version 1 until s6 runs migrate (plan §7.1), so doctor here reads 'config' WARN and 'level 0 declared: complete; weak: config' in the meantime, the in-memory path working as designed (the dry run measured '1 → 2: nothing to change (no paths.playbook)' plus the relaid note). Two wording changes from the plan accepted: the init row carries the exact migrate command, the kept outcome names the path. The twenty-five s2 strings go to the developer in one batch.

Rule 3: the recorded s3 split text ('hookCommand(rel) with the stage-1 text as past') and its checkpoint 'the hook command forms with tests' predate plan-review round 1 and are superseded by disposition 16: Claude's hook command and the git shims are unchanged in this stage, and s3 builds no hook-command change. The state's split text is the CLI's and stays as recorded; plan §4.4 and §10 are what s3 builds: HOSTS.claude keys, SKILLS, the link write and refuseLinks, init/pointers.mjs with ownership by text, doctor/hosts.mjs (host.pointers with the level rule), levels, the doctor fixture.

Rule 2 and rule 3: accepted as built, a row the plan's §4.4 table lacks: a link of our shape that does not resolve while the text init would write now does (written before install at the config-root form, the package then hoisted to the top) is init 'updated … pointed where cookwright is not installed; now links to <target>' and doctor WARN 'does not point where cookwright is installed (run npx cookwright init)'. The link is ours by text, so retargeting touches nothing of the user's, and the line names a step that clears it; a link that works is never touched. The closeout records the table's extra row.

Accepted as built: (1) the hook-command checkpoint was not built, per disposition 16; (3) the Windows pointer WARN names no backlog id yet, s5 adds the id when it opens the item (rule 3: no id invented before it exists); (4) no setup pointer is written until s5 ships skills/setup/SKILL.md, the derived expectations pick it up then, the Level 0 drift path is tested through the shipped seam; (5) doctor/hosts.mjs importing linkOnPath from init/files.mjs is the first doctor-to-init import, no cycle, changelog and migrate already import it there; (6) a linked parent directory is WARN like the user's own, and a file where the pointer's directory would be (ENOTDIR) is the user's entry (rule 2, chosen states); (7) codex reads '0 skills, 0 workflows' and init with codex in hosts throws in the pointers step until s4, as the s1 decision accepted. Commit 9a72ca4 went through with COOKWRIGHT_SKIP=doc-sync and its reason in the message (rule 8). The twenty-five s3 strings go to the developer in one batch.

Rule 3: whether the Codex SessionStart hook fires is unmeasured: under codex exec 0.145.0 no hook from .codex/hooks.json ran in three runs, trust bypassed or granted by config, so the file's shape is documented only. Nothing claims it: doctor's host.hook PASS names the file's text and leaves trust to the user, the README (s5) says the hook is confirmed only in an interactive Codex session after /hooks, and the QA leg checks it there when Codex is installed on the personal app. The developer's ~/.codex was not touched (rule 7).

Accepted as built (rule 3, rule 2): the Codex rules row writes nothing and mirrors Claude's skipped row, targeting the override ('not needed: nothing overrides AGENTS.md, which Codex reads natively'), naming the nearest override when one exists; an AGENTS.override.md anywhere from the invocation directory up through the config root is WARN as a chosen state, the note saying it replaces the AGENTS.md beside it (a nested override does not unread the root's block, and the WARN stands as the plan's chosen-state verdict); a global override under ~/.codex is outside the plan; with one host the host.rules and host.hook notes are unchanged, with several each note carries its host's name, worst first, SKIP ranking between WARN and PASS.

Rule 3: .codex/hooks.json is written at the config root like .claude/settings.json, and with a nested config root the Codex hook's cd to the work tree's top finds no cookwright.json and no package unless hoisted, the B-002 class; s5's backlog line for plan §9 (f) names the Codex hook beside Claude's. The twenty-one s4 strings go to the developer in one batch.

fix:route applies: finding 0 (rule 1, rule 3: host.pointers never runs git when doctor has no git or no work tree; tracking is then unverified and the ignored check is skipped, the pointer's verdict resting on the link alone; a test with hasGit false and one outside a work tree); finding 1 (rule 3: the playbook the bundle commands point at must be a regular file, statSync().isFile(), and a filesystem error while hashing any pointed-at file becomes the same one-line refusal, never an absolute path on the terminal); finding 2 (rule 1: migrate writes through a temporary file in the same directory and renameSync over cookwright.json, the mode kept, the temporary removed on failure, the pattern of lib/bundle/state.mjs, so 'not written' is always true); finding 3 (rule 3: the README's init bullet says the Codex hook file is written and that its firing is confirmed only in an interactive Codex session after /hooks, since no hook ran under codex exec; doctor's PASS note gains the same caveat in two words; s5 keeps that wording in its Codex paragraph; the QA leg on the personal app is the evidence, named as such); finding 4 (rule 5, rule 3: the 1→2 step pins paths.playbook to docs/playbook.md when the key is absent and a file exists there, outcome playbookPinned, 'the user's own', with a test, since a version-1 absent key meant that path); finding 5 (rule 2: only an AGENTS.override.md in the config root's own directory hides Level 0's rules and WARNs; a nested one is PASS with a note naming it, in doctor and in init's row, with tests; disposition 21's walk stays for the naming). Finding 6 (rule 3) needs no code: s6's fresh-session measurement opens one session in a subdirectory of this repo and records whether the named workflow and the skills resolve from the top's .claude/; if not, backlog §9 (f) gains the workflow placement beside the hook's.

Rule 2 (review:route finding 5, over the review disposition): kept as built. An AGENTS.override.md anywhere from the invocation directory up through the config root is a state the user chose, and Codex reads it in place of the AGENTS.md beside it, so WARN with the reason is rule 2's verdict for a chosen state even where the root's block stays in force; plan §4.4 and disposition 21 say so, and a change would be a plan revision for no user gain. Rule 5 and rule 3 (finding 4): accepted as a recorded deviation from plan §4.3's 'nothing else changes in 1→2': the step now pins paths.playbook to docs/playbook.md when a version-1 file had no key and a file is there (outcome playbookPinned), since the absent key meant that path under version 1. Backlog: E-027 (the interactive Codex hook measurement) and E-028 (named-workflow discovery from a nested config root) were opened by the fix session, so s5's §9 lines start at E-029; s6's fresh-session measurement covers E-028's Claude half. The fix session's git stash and pop restored the state file unchanged (verified by the CLI's own write afterwards). Commit 6f02b1e carried COOKWRIGHT_SKIP=doc-sync with its reason although no rule matched, harmless (rule 8). The three fix:route strings go to the developer with the s4 batch.

Accepted as built: (1) rule 2 and rule 3: the setup loop stops when every line is PASS or every line left is one the recipe says to stop at, not at 'complete' alone, since doctor prints 'complete; weak: config' while the in-memory migration is still open and the loop must run migrate; a line with no recipe ends the walkthrough; (2) rule 3: the recipe follows the statuses doctor emits today (backlog.ids WARN, rules.block newer WARN, tools.gitleaks SKIP) and names the rows the plan's table lacked (homes.backlog headings, a misdirected pointer, a hook path that is not a file, an env file not ignored, git absent, doctor's own could-not-run and unverified lines), held by a test that the skill names every registered check; (3) property 5 and rule 7: a cookwright backlog id (E-029, the Windows pointers) in the shipped skill is acceptable, the backlog being public in the open-source repo and holding nothing private; (4) E-014's narrowed line stays for s7, whose checkpoint it is; (5) rule 3 and disposition 23: the README's route to try an unpublished checkout is npm pack plus the tarball, never npm install <directory>, which links node_modules/cookwright outside the repo. On this repo doctor now reads the QA leg's three lines (config WARN migrated in memory, rules.block FAIL stale, host.pointers FAIL .claude/skills/setup missing) until s6 runs migrate and init, as plan §7 expects. The s5 strings (the setup skill's description and body, the bundle skill's level line, the block v3 sentence, the README sections) go to the developer in one batch.

decisions.source: implement:s6 report and the orchestrator's measurement, 2026-10-16 (plan §7.4, §8; review:route finding 6; E-028)
decisions.text: Rule 3, measured with one-shot Claude Code 2.1.301 sessions after s6's init: a fresh session at this repo's root listed setup, bundle, bundle-phase and docs-audit, all pointers into node_modules/cookwright, and its context carried 'SessionStart:startup hook success: cookwright doctor: level 0 complete'; a session started in packages/cookwright/src listed the same four, so skills and named workflows are found through the work tree top's .claude/ from a session below it. E-028 is closed on that evidence in the backlog (its Claude half; the hook placement for a nested config root stays B-002's). s6's two open questions accepted: migrate's parenthetical 'the file is rewritten in standard JSON layout, its indent kept' is the relaid note §7.1 expected, and the running session picking up the setup skill as soon as init wrote its pointer is noted as an observation, the fresh-session listing above being the measurement. s6 added no product string.

fix:setup applies: finding 3 (rule 1, rule 2: the setup loop gains a stop rule: a remedy that refuses, or a line that reads the same after its remedy, is shown with the command's output and stopped at, except that a refusal naming another check's line (init refusing on an invalid settings file) sends the loop to that line's recipe; a row for init's 'pointer … not written: this filesystem refuses symbolic links' that stops and names B-010); finding 1 (rule 3: an 'At the end' pass handles the guidance that sits on PASS rows, the no-gate-checks offer and the Codex /hooks trust, so an all-PASS readout still gets them); finding 4 (rule 3: README First run says a Codex user runs init --hosts codex or claude,codex, limits the session-start doctor line to Claude Code, and for Codex says to trust the hook with /hooks and run doctor by hand until E-027 is measured, step 5 pointing at the Codex section); finding 5 (rule 3: the README's Windows bullet says what the code does, a pointer checked out as a text file reads as 'your own' and only a pointer init could not write reads as the Windows WARN, and E-029's line gains that win32 should read a regular file holding our link text as the Windows state); finding 6 (rule 5: the recipe test checks a fixed list of doctor message fragments beside messages.doctor, so the exhaustive table cannot go stale silently). Finding 0 was rejected by the verifier (the README's release block is for a user's app repo, where the root package is the package; this repo's own release is the plan's §8 instruction). Finding 2 (rule 8, the doc-sync letter): no change; the plan sequenced s5 as skill, block, then README and backlog, the window lies inside one unmerged branch, and a docSync rule tying the skills and the block to the README is backlogged as wanted once (rule 6).
